Jigging is one of the oldest and most popular fishing techniques and gives the appearance of an injured fish.
To jig, cast out and let your jig sink to the bottom. Snap or flick your rod sideways or up and down, then let the jig sink back to the bottom.
Jigging is a popular inshore and offshore method that can lead to success with many different species.

bait.name: Plastic worms
lines: A soft plastic worm is a classic bass lure.
It is often fished on a Texas rig, Carolina rig or drop-shot rig, so the hook is hidden and the worm moves slowly on the bottom.
Fish it slowly near weeds, docks and fallen trees.

bait.name: Crankbaits
lines: A crankbait is a hard lure with a lip that makes it dive when you reel.
A bigger lip dives deeper. Cast it, reel steadily, and bump it off cover or the bottom.

bait.name: Spinnerbaits
lines: A spinnerbait has a skirted head and one or two spinning blades on a wire arm.
It is often reeled steadily past weeds, docks and wood, because the wire arm helps keep the hook from snagging.

bait.name: Swimbaits
lines: A swimbait is a soft or hard lure shaped like a small fish.
A paddle tail swims with a steady reel; fish it at the depth where the fish are.

bait.name: Topwater frogs
lines: A hollow-body frog floats and is worked over thick weeds and lily pads, where other lures snag.
Bass often hit it from underneath, so give a short pause before you set the hook.

bait.name: Nightcrawlers
lines: Nightcrawlers are large worms sold at bait shops.
Thread one on a hook and fish it on the bottom or under a bobber. Many freshwater fish will take one.

bait.name: Salmon eggs
lines: Salmon eggs are a common trout bait.
Use a small hook and light line, and let the bait drift through pools or settle near the bottom.

bait.name: Corn and dough baits
lines: Canned corn and dough-type baits are cheap, easy baits for stocked trout and catfish.
Mold the dough around a small hook or put a few kernels on it.
Some states do not allow corn as bait in some waters. Check your state rules first.

bait.name: Squid
lines: A strip of squid is a tough cut bait that stays on the hook.
Fish it on the bottom for snapper and other bottom fish.

bait.name: Chum
lines: Chum is bait or ground fish put in the water to bring fish to your spot.
Drift your hook with a small piece of the same bait in the chum so it looks like part of the meal.

bait.name: Leeches
lines: Leeches are a common live bait for walleye in northern waters.
Fish one on a jig or a slow-moving rig near the bottom.

bait.name: Eels
lines: A live eel is a large bait for big fish such as striped bass and cobia.
Use a strong leader and a hook sized for the bait.
